# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure and find the labeling logic.

Here is a full map of the repository.

## 1. Project structure, language, framework, build/test

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Language | Python 3.9 (Dockerfile pins `python:3.9.2`) |
| Framework | Flask (v1.1.2) + pandas (1.2.4) + numpy + scipy/scikit-learn + fuzzywuzzy/python-Levenshtein |
| Repo root | `/app` — only `.gitignore`, `Dockerfile`, `categorizationapp/` |
| Package | `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/` (installed via `pip3 install -e .` from `/app/categorizationapp`) |
| Packaging | `/app/categorizationapp/setup.py` (no `requirements.txt`, no `pyproject.toml`, no CI config, no Makefile) |
| Run/build | `docker build` on `/app/Dockerfile`; runtime cmd: `gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app`. Dev: `python -m categorizationapp` / `app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=9898)` (`__init__.py:30-31`) |
| Test command | **None. There is no test framework, no test files, no pytest/unittest reference anywhere in the repo.** |
| Git | Single branch `main`, single commit `0a1b6a3 "import codebase"` |
| Total code | ~10.2k lines of Python across 53 files |

### Entry points
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py` — Flask app factory, logging, request timing hooks.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` (936 lines) — three routes:
  - `GET /` — health.
  - `POST /recurrentTransactions` → `recurrent_transactions()`.
  - `POST /categorizeTransaction` — the main enrichment endpoint. Payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`. `pd.json_normalize` turns rows into a DataFrame; expected row columns include `description` (the narration), `remark` (the reference field), `amount`, `type` (`DEBIT`/`CREDIT`), `balanceAfterTransaction`, `transactionDate`.
  - Controller is a giant `if bank == ... elif` chain (35 near-identical ~20-line blocks, one per bank) that always runs the same pipeline.

### Enrichment pipeline order (per bank block in Controller.py)
1. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(...)` — bank-specific: sets `transactionCategory`, seeds `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, and extracts `partyName` (+ `party2`) from the narration.
2. If `acc_type == "CREDIT_CARD"`: `card_clean_names()` then `card_purpose()`.
3. `purpose(transactions, accountType)` — generic subcategory + merchantType rules.
4. `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` — canonical payee/merchant naming.
5. If `accountHolder` present: `internal_payment(...)`.
6. If `acc_type == "SAVING"`: `salary_detection(...)`.
7. If `isPFMEnabled`: `pfm_categorization()` then `simple_description()`.
8. Response: `transactions.to_json(orient='records')`.

## 2. Where enrichment / labeling logic lives

All under `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/`.

### Core generic enrichment (UtilityScripts/)
| File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | 300 | **Main subcategory + merchantType deriver** for SAVING/CURRENT. Builds `conditions_choices` lists of `[boolean mask, label]` and applies `np.select(...)` to write `transactionSubcategory`, then `transactionCategory` overrides (TDS/TAX/REFUND/CASHBACK/FD/INTEREST), then `merchantType` (NBFC, HFC, Pay Later, Flight, Electricity, Mutual Fund, ...), then a final blank-out pass for reversals/charges/bounces. Matches on `description`, `partyName`, and `party2`. |
| `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | **1971** | **Payee/counterparty canonicalization.** Hundreds of `[regex match on description/partyName/party2 → canonical "Airtel DTH"/"BESCOM"/"Dream11"/... ]` rules; ends with normalization fixes (Pvt Ltd/Ltd/Corporation/Restaurant casing, ICICI/HDFC/SBI/RBL uppercasing, salary stop-word stripping) and derived `merchantType`/`transactionSubcategory` tweaks. |
| `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | 191 | Shared regex vocabulary: `SALARY`, `NOT_SAL`, `SAL_IMPS`, `SALARY_DISB`, `REIMBURSE`, `LOAN`, `LOAN_REP`, `LOAN_REP1`, `LOAN_REP_AUTO`, `LOAN_REP_DESC`, `LOAN_DESC`, `BANK_LOAN*`, `NEGATE_LOAN*`, `CREDIT_CARD`, `INSURANCE`, `INVEST`, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, `INSUFF_BOUNCE`, `INTERNAL_PAY` (self-transfer), `RENT`, `RENT_INCOME`, `TRF_TO_WALLET`/`TRF_FRM_WALLET`, `TAX*`, `POS_STL`, `POS_RENT`, `EMI_MOR`, plus merchantType vocab (`NBFC`, `HFC`, `PAYLATER`, `P2P`, `VEHIC_LOAN`, `GAMING`, `ELECTRICITY`, `PMT_GTW`, ...). |
| `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | 432 | ~308 bank-specific narration parsing patterns, e.g. `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10`, `HDFC_FT_PATTERN1..7`, `FT_PATTERN8..11` (61 `FT_*`), `SBI_*` (46: `SBI_CP_*` POS, `SBI_AUTOPAY*`, `SBI_INB_*`, `SBI_IMPS_*`, `SBI_BP_*`), `PNB_*`, `UB_*`, `UCO_*`, `NEFT_*`, `IMPS_*`, `CHQ_*`, `ECS_*`, `REVERSAL_*`, `ACC_VERIF`, `HDFC_POS_PATTERN`, `POS_REFUND_PATTERN`, `SI_PATTERN`. |
| `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | 66 | Narration-splitting helpers used everywhere: `clean_input_df`, `sep_by_` (`/`), `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_wave`, `sep_by_star`, `sep_by_comma`, `sep_by_colon`, `sep_by_under`, bracket variants, `fuzzy_match` (fuzzywuzzy ratio), and `py_extract(series, pat, index)` (null-safe regex extract). |
| `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` | 217 | Statistical salary/reimbursement labeling: Levenshtein distance matrix over normalized `partyName` → `scipy` hierarchical clustering (`linkage`/`cut_tree`, height 1.5) into `Group_ID`; then multi-scenario heuristics (mode amount, party frequency vs month frequency, second salary, reimbursement via `< 0.3 * max`). Wrapped in try/except returning `None` on failure. |
| `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` | 62 | Self-transfer detection: normalizes `accountHolder` and `partyName` (strips Mr/M/S/Pvt/Ltd etc.), fuzzy-matches (threshold 75) → `transactionSubcategory = "INTERNAL_PAYMENT"` + `isInternalPayment` flag. |
| `UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` | 206 | Second-level PFM taxonomy: `pfmCategoryOne`, `pfmCategoryTwo`, `pfmCategoryType` (EXPENSE/INCOME/TRANSFER) derived from `transactionSubcategory`/`transactionCategory`/`merchantType`. |
| `UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` | 19 | Builds `pfmSimpleDescription` = `partyName - <TransactionCategory enum value>`. Note: uses `transactions.transactionCategory.get(0)` — looks buggy (uses row 0's category for all rows). |
| `UtilityScripts/RecurrentTxns.py` | 25 | Same clustering as SalaryDetection to group recurring payees into `Group_ID`. |
| `UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py` | 158 | Credit-card variant of `purpose()` (description-only matching). |
| `UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py` | 927 | Credit-card variant of `clean_names()`. |
| `UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | 171 | `TransactionCategory` enum: 170 labels (`CHEQUE_RETURN="Cheque Bounce"`, `ECS_BOUNCE`, `REVERSAL`, `UPI_REVERSAL`, `NEFT_RETURN`, `OUTWARD_BOUNCE`, `INWARD_BOUNCE`, `ATM_REVERSAL`, `SALARY`, `TPT`, ...). |
| `UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` | 136 | `TransactionSubcategory` enum: 135 labels (`SALARY`, `SALARY_DISBURSED`, `REIMBURSEMENT`, `INTERNAL_PAYMENT`, `LOAN_REPAYMENT`, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE`, `CHEQUE_BOUNCE`, `RENT_INCOME`, ...). |

### Bank-specific narration parsers (BankScripts/, 35 files)
Each exposes `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType[, accountHolder])`. Largest/most representative:
- `BankScripts/Kotak.py` (327), `BankScripts/HDFC.py` (276), `BankScripts/Indusind.py` (263), `BankScripts/IDBI.py` (247), `BankScripts/ICICI.py` (245), `BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py` (235), `BankScripts/Canara.py` (201), `BankScripts/StandardCharted.py` (208), `BankScripts/SBI.py` (193), `BankScripts/PNB.py` (192), `BankScripts/Axis.py` (188), `BankScripts/BOB.py` (167), `BankScripts/CityUnion.py` (162), `BankScripts/Citi.py` (151), `BankScripts/UnionBank.py` (152), `BankScripts/RBL.py` (147), `BankScripts/YES.py` (142), `BankScripts/Syndicate.py` (141), `BankScripts/KarurVyasa.py` (130), `BankScripts/Federal.py` (112), plus `Andhra`, `AuSmallFinanceBank`, `Bandhan`, `BOI`, `Central`, `DCB`, `IDFC`, `Indian`, `Karnataka`, `Paytm`, `Saraswat`, `SouthIndian`, `SVC`, `TamilnadMerchantile`, `UCO`.

Typical file shape (see `BankScripts/HDFC.py`):
1. `transactionCategory` via ~90 `[regex on description/remark/amount/type → CATEGORY]` rules, default `"TRANSFER"` (covers ATM withdrawal, reversals, UPI/IMPS/NEFT/RTGS/TPT, cheque paid/deposit/return, auto-payment & bounce, charges, FD/RD redemption, payment-gateway routing, plus row-adjacency rules using `.shift()` for reversal/bounce pairs).
2. Seeds `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName` to `""`.
3. `transactionSubcategory` seeding rules (LOAN, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INVESTMENT, SALARY, SALARY_DISBURSED, CREDIT_CARD_PAYMENT, FOREX_TXN, GST, INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE, INTERNAL_PAYMENT).
4. `partyName` extraction: ~70 rules combining `sep_by_dash/sep_by_/sep_by_colon` positional splits and `py_extract` with `*_PATTERN` regexes from `BankRegexConstants`, plus `SAL_STOP_WORDS`, `POS_STOP_WORDS`, `NAMES_STOP_WORDS` cleanup; then `.str.title()` and per-bank clean-up rules; finally `party2 = partyName` with spaces removed.

## 3. Existing tests for that logic

**There are none.** Verified by:
- `find /app -iname "*test*"` (excluding `.git`) → no results.
- Grep for `pytest|unittest|nose` across all `.py`/`.txt`/`.cfg`/`.toml`/`.ini` → no matches.
- No `tests/` dir, no `conftest.py`, no `tox.ini`, no CI workflow, no fixture/sample data (`.gitignore` even excludes `*.csv`).

The only test-adjacent artifacts are commented-out debug blocks labeled `# For testing purpose only` (dendrogram plots) in `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py:27-32` and `UtilityScripts/RecurrentTxns.py:16-21`.

## Notes relevant to adding tests or changing logic
- All logic is pure `pandas` DataFrame transformation: functions take a DataFrame and return a DataFrame, so they are directly unit-testable without Flask — except `Purpose.py`, `CleanName.py`, `CardPurpose.py`, `CardCleanNames.py`, which `from categorizationapp import app` (import-time Flask app creation) for logging.
- Required input columns per row: `description`, `remark`, `amount`, `type`, `balanceAfterTransaction`, `transactionDate` (`%d/%m/%Y`, used by SalaryDetection).
- Ordering matters: bank script must run before `purpose()`/`clean_names()` because those read `partyName`/`party2`/`transactionCategory`.
- Dependency-version sensitivity: Flask 1.1.2 with pinned `itsdangerous==2.0.1`, `Jinja2<3.1.0`, `Werkzeug<2.1.0`; `np.select` semantics (first matching condition wins) is the core dispatch mechanism throughout.

"""Direct in-process harness for the categorization pipeline.

Mirrors the per-bank pipeline order used by Controller.categorizeTransaction
without going through Flask/JSON serialisation.
"""
import sys

import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, '/app/categorizationapp')

from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts import AppUtil                      # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.Purpose import purpose              # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CleanName import clean_names        # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CardCleanNames import card_clean_names  # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CardPurpose import card_purpose     # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.InternalPayment import internal_payment  # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.SalaryDetection import salary_detection   # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.PFMCategorization import pfm_categorization  # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.SimpleDescription import simple_description  # noqa: E402

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions      # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions    # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.SBI import categorize_SBI_transactions        # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Axis import categorize_Axis_transactions      # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Kotak import categorize_Kotak_transactions    # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.PNB import categorize_PNB_transactions        # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.DCB import categorize_DCB_transactions        # noqa: E402
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.UCO import categorize_UCO_transactions        # noqa: E402

BANKS = {
    'HDFC': categorize_HDFC_transactions,
    'ICICI': categorize_ICICI_transactions,
    'SBI': categorize_SBI_transactions,
    'AXIS': categorize_Axis_transactions,
    'KOTAK': categorize_Kotak_transactions,
    'PNB': categorize_PNB_transactions,
    'DCB': categorize_DCB_transactions,
    'UCO': categorize_UCO_transactions,
}


def run(bank, acc_type, rows, accountHolder="", pfm=False, do_salary=True):
    transactions = pd.json_normalize(rows)
    transactions = AppUtil.clean_input_df(transactions)
    transactions = BANKS[bank](transactions, acc_type)
    if acc_type == "CREDIT_CARD":
        transactions = card_clean_names(transactions)
        transactions = card_purpose(transactions)
    transactions = purpose(transactions, acc_type)
    transactions = clean_names(transactions, acc_type, bank)
    if accountHolder and accountHolder.strip() != "":
        transactions = internal_payment(transactions, accountHolder, bank, acc_type)
    if acc_type == "SAVING" and do_salary:
        result = salary_detection(transactions)
        transactions = transactions if result is None else result
    if pfm:
        transactions = pfm_categorization(transactions)
        transactions = simple_description(transactions)
    return transactions


def row(desc, amount, ttype, remark="", bal=10000.0, date="01/04/2022"):
    return {
        "description": desc,
        "remark": remark,
        "amount": amount,
        "type": ttype,
        "balanceAfterTransaction": bal,
        "transactionDate": date,
    }


def show(df, cols=("description", "type", "transactionCategory",
                   "transactionSubcategory", "partyName", "merchantType")):
    cols = [c for c in cols if c in df.columns]
    with pd.option_context('display.max_colwidth', 70, 'display.width', 260):
        print(df[cols].to_string())

steps.message:
All five complaints traced to five single-token faults, each inside an otherwise-correct rule. Fixed:

| Digest complaint | Location | Fault | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| All-numeric reference credit no longer a cheque deposit | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:100` | `remark.str.len().eq(15)` contradicted its own regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` (needs 16 chars) → rule was dead, row fell through to default `TRANSFER` | `.eq(16)` |
| Bare 6-digit narration lost the salary sub-tag | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:124` | `accountType=="SAVINGS"` — the API only ever passes `SAVING` (every other rule in the repo uses `SAVING`) | `"SAVING"` |
| Direction-word-led transfers give empty/wrong counterparty | `BankScripts/ICICI.py:159` | `py_extract(pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned the direction word, not the name → `"From"`, or `""` after the 1–2 char blanking rule | `index=1` |
| 4-field slash bill transfer lifts the numeric reference | `BankScripts/ICICI.py:147` | `BIL/INFT/<ref>/<payee>` (`count("/")==3`) read field 2 (the reference) instead of the final field | `sep_by_(desc,3,4)` |
| Offsetting credit after its matching debit recorded as a bounce | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:98` | `description.shift(periods=2)` while every other term in the pair rule uses `shift(1)`; the REVERSAL rule could not fire, so the row fell to the next rule, `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` | `shift(periods=1)` |

Verification (out-of-tree harness in `/tmp/opencode`, nothing added to the repo):

- Built a 238-row synthetic corpus across HDFC, ICICI and 6 untouched banks (SAVING/CURRENT), snapshotted every output column before and after.
- Exactly 17 rows changed — all of them the digest's edge shapes. Near-miss neighbours held steady: 15-/17-char remarks, non-11-zero prefixes, debit side, 5- and 7-digit narrations, `123456` on a CURRENT account, debit/credit pairs with differing amounts, credit-before-debit ordering, genuine `SI` auto-payment bounces (still `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`), and the 5-field `BIL/INFT/.../RENT/...` variant.
- Smoke-tested all 35 banks × 4 account types through `POST /categorizeTransaction` with the PFM path enabled: 0 failures.
- Static sweep confirms no remaining siblings of these fault classes: one `str.len().eq` (fixed), all 22 `shift(periods=…)` now `1`, and `accountType` compared only against real values (`SAVING`/`CURRENT`/`CREDIT_CARD`/`OVER_DRAFT`).

One consequence worth flagging: the restored cheque-deposit row (`MAHESH KUMAR`, 16-digit remark) now yields an empty `partyName`. That is inherent to the rule firing, not a choice — HDFC's `partyName` rule at line 215 that copied the description is gated on `transactionCategory == "TRANSFER"`, and cheque deposits are expected to take their name from the MICR patterns instead. It would be the same under any repair that revives line 100.
